classification.difficultyReason: The parts explicitly guide the two midpoint-vector expressions and their equality; the remaining decision is to recognise the equal, parallel opposite-side criterion for a parallelogram.

content.prompt:
In the diagram to the right, $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral. The points $P,Q,R$ and $S$ are the midpoints of $AB,BC,CD$ and $DA$ respectively.

Let $\overrightarrow{AB}=\underset{\sim}{a}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}=\underset{\sim}{b}$, $\overrightarrow{AD}=\underset{\sim}{d}$ and $\overrightarrow{DC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$.

spec.description: Unshaded irregular quadrilateral with labelled vertices and midpoint dots. Single, double, triple and quadruple ticks distinguish the four midpoint relationships. No diagonals or midpoint-joining segments are supplied. Ordinary source marks are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: P is the midpoint of AB, Q of BC, R of CD and S of DA. Coordinates specify schematic appearance only and introduce no numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry is visible in the question; no solution marks are included.

answer.short: Both sums equal $\overrightarrow{AC}$ by the triangle addition law.
answer.worked:
By the triangle addition law,

$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{AC}=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b},\\\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DC}&=\overrightarrow{AC}=\underset{\sim}{d}+\underset{\sim}{c}.\end{align*}$$

Hence $\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}=\underset{\sim}{d}+\underset{\sim}{c}$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Deduce that the quadrilateral $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.

answer.short: $PQ$ and $SR$ are parallel and equal in length, so $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: Since $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\overrightarrow{SR}$, the opposite sides $PQ$ and $SR$ are parallel and equal in length. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides parallel and equal is a parallelogram. Hence $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.
